Benchmarks and quantization impact on latency and cost
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-08-24 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Hydra Head of ML), Priya (Hydra CTO), Liam (Hydra FinOps), Sasha (Hydra Security)

Summary (auto): Quick QBR to align on SLA targets, committed capacity pricing, security signoffs, and a plan for a dedicated soak test. Action items captured.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: SLA rebalance, cost model updates, private/vpc checklist and then bench and canary plan. is that ok?
[00:18] Jordan (Hydra): yep that sounds good. we've got some new traffic patterns since the last quarter, so figure we should rebaseline.
[00:30] Priya (Hydra): hey, sorry I'm late, had another meeting — but I wanted to highlight we need more predictability on monthly committed spend.
[00:40] Samir: totally, this call is exactly to get that scoped. Liam, do you want to surface the main finance constraints?
[00:49] Liam (Hydra FinOps): sure — our big ask is a firm per-token cap for the dedicated pool, or at least a band. spikes have cost us 40% more last quarter, and we need guardrails to avoid surprises.
[01:05] Maya (Redwood SE): quick note — we saw the traffic shape, and a mix of short chat sessions and long context requests; batching/kv-cache will help but there's explicit tradeoffs with latency SLOs.
[01:22] Jordan: when you say kv-cache, do you mean K-V cache? last time I heard someone call it K-V cash on a call which made me laugh.
[01:30] Maya: (laugh) yeah K-V cache. sorry if transcription eats that. we can tune prefix caching for repeated prompts which reduces per-token work.
[01:45] Sasha (Security): from compliance, the SOC2 artifacts and KMS key rotation policies are blockers until we get them in place for private deployments. we need a clear audit window.
[01:58] Diego (Redwood CSM): understood. we'll share the SOC2 pack and a network diagram. Samir will follow up on KMS integration notes.
[02:12] Priya: big question — dedicated vs hosted. can you re-explain the differences in guarantees? we keep hearing both from sales and the infra team.
[02:25] Samir: sure. hosted is consumption-based with best-effort routing and standard SLAs; dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with stronger latency/throughput guarantees and an SLA backstop. dedicated also lets you pin model versions and control KV cache persistence.
[02:43] Liam: ok, but dedicated was more expensive in our early pilot. can you show how batching and quantization would change that math?
[02:55] Maya: yes. we ran a sample on 8k seq with int8 quantization — on that workload the per-token cost dropped ~28% and latency p95 stayed within your 300ms SLO for short prompts, but long-context tails did increase by ~20ms due to dequant overhead.
[03:18] Jordan: can you share that bench spreadsheet? I want the raw numbers.
[03:23] Maya: we'll share the bench (link) — note it's a lab run, real-world will vary with prefix reuse.
[03:32] Priya: about SLA penalties — what are your proposed thresholds and remedies? we need clear escalation steps.
[03:41] Samir: proposed structure: uptime SLA 99.5% for dedicated with credits tiered at 99.0 and 98.0; latency SLOs per route; and an agreed canary rollback policy. if we breach, credits and prioritized remediation are triggered.
[03:58] Liam: would acceptance criteria include a soak test? like 48-72 hour ramp with production traffic shape?
[04:08] Diego: yeah that's reasonable. Hydra asked for a 90-minute soak earlier — I'd suggest a staged soak: internal 90m then 48h external soak for the dedicated pool.
[04:19] Jordan: can Redwood support region-specific capacity? we need us-west2 and eu-west1 pinned for data residency.
[04:28] Samir: yes — dedicated pools can be region pinned. for geo routing we can set policy to prefer region; fallback to hosted in emergencies.
[04:40] Sasha: on encryption — we need to know whether Redwood will hold the KMS keys or if we can bring-your-own. and if audit logs include per-request key id.
[04:50] Maya: we support BYOK via customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM; audit logs include key id metadata but we'll confirm the retention window.
[05:00] Priya: great, put that in writing. we also want RBAC scoping so only a small set of services can request model rollouts.
[05:12] Samir: that's standard — role mappings via SSO/SAML, and RBAC in the console. Diego will prepare the mapping template.
[05:22] Liam: another finance angle — if we commit to 6 months reserved capacity, can we lock a discounted rate for burst usage? last time bursts were billed at list.
[05:33] Samir: we can offer a reserved tier with overflow bursting at a reduced premium compared to on-demand; I'll include a few pricing bands in the proposal.
[05:44] Jordan: one technical worry — we've seen tokenization variance across model variants; if we fallback to a smaller model in region, outputs change. how do you handle quality regressions?
[05:56] Maya: we recommend a model compatibility matrix and automated evals. Redwood Optimize can run prompt suites and flag regressions; automatic fallback policy can be set to avoid quality dropouts for critical routes.
[06:12] Jordan: ok that's important. please share a sample eval report.
[06:18] Maya: yes — will attach sample eval and the configuration for canary thresholds.
[06:26] Priya: timeline — we need this locked before our next product launch in mid-September. is that feasible?
[06:33] Samir: assuming signoff on SLA and PO by end of August, yes — we can schedule provisioning and a soak in early September.
[06:43] Liam: procurement will need the contract terms. any special clauses around data residency and deletion?
[06:49] Samir: standard addendum covers data residency and deletion; we'll flag the retention and deletion APIs. I'll get legal to send a redline-friendly version.
[06:58] Sasha: one more on security — need details on how telemetry is sampled and where traces land. we can't have cross-tenant leakage.
[07:09] Maya: telemetry is sampled per-customer token-level metrics; traces are isolated and stored under your tenancy. we'll include the retention period and export controls.
[07:22] Jordan: can we talk about model governance — pinning versions, automatic rollbacks, labeling of experimental models?
[07:31] Diego: we've got a model rollout page in the console where you can pin, tag, and create canary percentages. rollbacks can be automated on error or eval regression.
[07:42] Priya: we'd like a governance matrix shared — which teams approve rollouts, who owns QA.
[07:49] Samir: we'll share a template governance matrix; you can map approvers.
[07:56] Liam: back to cost — show us an example per-route breakdown with batching and cache effects, e.g., route-a vs route-b. high level numbers will help procurement.
[08:08] Maya: we'll produce a per-route example and a sensitivity table: batching windows 10-50ms vs per-request latency and token cost.
[08:18] Jordan: about quantization — you mentioned int8 earlier, do you support int4? are there quality tradeoffs?
[08:25] Maya: we support int8 and experimental int4 for some model families; int4 gives more savings but can introduce subtle quality regressions on rare prompts. we'll quantify in the bench.
[08:38] Priya: ok please call out which route classes are safe for int4.
[08:44] Maya: will do.
[08:48] Samir: quick callout — customers sometimes ask for a cost-protection clause if model families deprecate; we'll add a note about migration credits for model deprecation events.
[08:59] Jordan: nice. that eases risk.
[09:05] Diego: let's talk deliverables and dates — Samir are you good to own the proposal?
[09:11] Samir: yes. I'll own proposal and SLA. Maya will own bench artifacts. Diego will own onboarding checklist and governance template.
[09:21] Priya: from legal side we need a PO and want to review a draft by 8/27.
[09:27] Samir: noted.
[09:31] Liam: question — if the dedicated pool is underutilized, do we get credits or ability to shift to hosted?
[09:40] Samir: there are two levers: commit smoothing (we can apply credits if sustained underutilization over a billing period) or transfer to burstable pools. we'll include the smoothing policy.
[09:51] Jordan: on the soak test — what telemetry and acceptance criteria do you want from us?
[09:58] Maya: we need traffic replay shape, success rates, latency p95 target, and a regression threshold on eval metrics. ideally you give us a representative dataset.
[10:10] Jordan: we can provide a scrubbed traffic sample and the critical prompt set.
[10:16] Sasha: also include a list of IP ranges for the VPC peer so security can pre-approve.
[10:22] Diego: noted. we'll send the VPC peering doc.
[10:28] Priya: any competitive risk we should be aware of if we take dedicated? like lock-in concerns?
[10:36] Samir: we try to minimize lock-in — models are open-model friendly and exports are possible. dedicated gives portability, but we'll discuss exit terms in the contract.
[10:47] Liam: can you provide a 12-month cost projection for three scenarios: conservative, mid, aggressive usage?
[10:55] Maya: yes; we'll produce a projection and sensitivity ranges.
[11:02] Jordan: last technical thing — how do you handle long context KV cache persistence across restarts? critical for our docs summarization flows.
[11:11] Maya: we persist KV cache for pinned sessions in the dedicated pool; there's a TTL and you can snapshot/restore. we'll include the limits in the doc.
[11:23] Priya: ok good.
[11:27] Samir: quick recap before we close: 1) Samir to send SLA + proposal by 8/27, 2) Maya to share bench and eval artifacts by 8/28, 3) Diego to send onboarding/VPC checklist by 8/29, 4) Hydra to confirm audit POC by 8/30. anyone missing?
[11:41] Jordan: that's right. also please add the model governance matrix and a clear rollback runbook.
[11:47] Diego: noted.
[11:50] Priya: thanks all. one more please: include the PO template in the next email so procurement can pre-fill.
[11:59] Samir: will include. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in writing and set the soak calendar.
[12:06] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K-V cash, VPC peeing) cleaned minimally; original export included some speaker mislabels.
